nonvacuity: Take n=2, independent fair assignments and Y_i(z)=z_i. This is a positive finite experiment, has no interference and interior marginals, is Bernoulli, and has ATE=EATE=ADSE=1. scratch/Check.lean compiles the fair law, Bernoulli property, no interference, Regular(2,4,1), and EATE=1 for this example.

For n=2 with zero outcomes, the full-cube interference and dependence matrices are the identity. Thus C1=C2=Cinf=dAvg=1 and the chain holds with positive denominators. scratch/Check.lean compiles the structural relations and C1=dAvg=1. scratch/Enumerate.py additionally checks all 4096 directed interference structures with mandatory diagonal on four units.

A nonconstant-effect instance uses n=2, Y_1(z)=z_1(1-2z_2), Y_2(z)=0, K=1, P the point mass at (0,0), and Q the point mass at (0,1). The effects are bounded by 1 on the full cube; the two EATEs are 1/2 and -1/2, and TV(P,Q)=1. All hypotheses are satisfied without positive conditioning probabilities being needed.

Use n=2, Y_1(z)=z_1(1-2z_2), Y_2(z)=0 and K=1, with any design. Then tau(z)=(1-2z_2)/2 is nonconstant, the full-cube effect bound holds, Cinf=2, and r=1 or r=2 gives meaningful finite ground distances and constants. For r=1 the assignments (0,0),(0,1) have tau difference 1 and right-hand bound 2.

Use the same two-unit nonconstant-effect outcomes as T37, K=1, r=1, P=delta_(0,0), Q=delta_(0,1). The unique coupling has expected L1 distance 1, so wasserstein=1; the EATE difference is 1 and the claimed bound is 2. Coupling nonemptiness and bounded costs are explicit in this instance and hold generally by the product coupling and finiteness.

The target is not mathematically empty: take n_t=2(t+1), complete randomization of n_t/2 units, and Y_i(z)=z_1(z_i-1/2) for every unit. Then Regular holds with k=2,q=4,s=1, dAvg=n_t, EATE=1/2, and HT=Hajek=z_1 on support, so both errors have absolute value 1/2. The omission is nevertheless justified on the supplied record: the only credited row is declared wrong_credit and expressly unusable even by component extraction. The Hájek completion defect is material for arbitrary designs, which can put all their mass on the two empty-arm assignments. This judgment accepts the supplied row-status declaration without inspecting an unavailable formalization.

Take n_t=2(t+1), independent fair assignments and zero outcomes. RegularSequence holds with k=2,q=4,s=1; I=D=identity, dAvg=1 and dAvg/n_t tends to zero. The retained HT conclusions therefore have genuine hypotheses. All-false and all-true assignments each have mass 2^(-n_t)>0, confirming the exact domain issue disclosed for the omitted Hájek conclusions. A two-unit instance and a supported empty arm compile in scratch/Check.lean.

Take n_t=2(t+1), zero outcomes and the uniform complete design with m_t=t+1 treated units. Use fixed p=1/2, so floor(p*n_t)=m_t with 0<m_t<n_t at every t. Marginals are 1/2 and RegularSequence(2,4,1) holds. The mandatory-diagonal counts give dAvg=C1=1, hence both restricted interference and C1=o(sqrt(n_t)). Both weighted arms equal n_t on support. The n=2 complete law and its supported arms compile in scratch/Check.lean.

Both design branches are inhabited: for n_t=2(t+1), use zero outcomes and either independent fair assignments or uniform complete randomization of n_t/2 units. Both have RegularSequence(2,4,1), dAvg=1=O(1), and positive rate 1/sqrt(n_t). The complete branch has both arms nonempty on support; the Bernoulli branch has supported empty arms. Finite versions of both laws compile in scratch/Check.lean.

Take n_t=2(t+1), pair consecutive units, independently randomize one treated unit per pair, and set all outcomes to zero. RegularSequence(2,4,1) holds. I=D=identity, dAvg=1, e_ij is exactly the partner indicator, eAvg=1 and rSum=0. All three required little-o conditions hold, and both weighted arms equal n_t on support. scratch/Check.lean compiles the n=2 fixed-point-free pairing, paired design and supported-arm property.

Use n_t=2(t+1), consecutive independent randomized pairs and zero outcomes. Take k=2 and q=s=infinity. Both observed and forced potential outcomes are uniformly bounded, so the global moment maxima exist and are attained at infinity. Here dAvg=1, alphaExt=1/4 (only partner pairs contribute), alphaInt=0, and all required ratios to n_t tend to zero. SupportedArms holds, so this witness inhabits the Hájek part as well as HT. The pairing, finite law and supported arms compile at n=2 in scratch/Check.lean. The stronger global-maximality and Hájek-domain requirements are accurately disclosed in the docstring and record.

The same zero-outcome paired sequence as T45 satisfies RegularMix with k=2 and q=s=infinity. The observed exponent infinity is attained at that very k and every candidate exponent is at most infinity. Also dAvg=1, alphaExt=1/4 and SupportedArms holds, so the mixing, restricted-interference and conditional Hájek hypotheses all hold together. No maximal potential exponent or separation condition is needed by this statement. The Hájek support restriction and use of the fixed-k observed maximum are accurately disclosed.

Take n_t=2(t+1), independent fair assignments and Y_i(z)=z_i. RegularSequence(2,4,1), q>=4, Bernoulli and no interference all hold; dAvg=1, msq=1 and B1=B2=0. Thus the specialization has a nonzero moving center. The two-unit regularity and msq=1 compile in scratch/Check.lean. Independently, scratch/Enumerate.py verifies the exact expectation identity behind the general B1/B2 decomposition in 100 rational Bernoulli examples with probabilities 1/3,2/5,3/4.

Take n_t=2(t+1), independent fair assignments and Y_i(z)=z_i. RegularSequence(2,4,1), Bernoulli and restricted interference hold. Each unit HT contribution is 2Z_i, so sigma_i^2=1 for every i and sdSigmaSq=0. Also dAvg=dRMS=1; the required little-o quotient is identically zero with denominator one. The finite regularity and nonzero effect witness compile in scratch/Check.lean.

For n_t=2(t+1), independent fair assignments and Y_i(z)=z_i, RegularSequence(2,4,1) holds, dAvg=dMax=1, and msq=1. Thus the first alternative has quotient 1/sqrt(n_t) tending to zero, while the second has restricted interference and the eventual lower bound msq>=1. Both alternatives are genuinely satisfiable. The two-unit Bernoulli, regularity and msq=1 checks compile in scratch/Check.lean.

The same fair Bernoulli sequence with Y_i(z)=z_i has D=identity, hence lambdaMax=dAvg=dMax=1 and msq=1. Both sufficient alternatives hold, with the first quotient 1/sqrt(n_t) and the second lower bound one. The finite spectral sandwich is also attained at both ends. For every positive n its unit sphere is nonempty (a coordinate vector lies on it), so lambdaMax does not exploit an empty or unbounded supremum.

For an explicit nontrivial instance choose n_t=(t+2)^2, fair independent assignments, k=2, alpha=1/2 and x=0. Let h=t+2, f(z)=(2z_1-1)z_2, Dbar=2-1/h, and set Y_i(z)=sqrt(Dbar)(z_i-1/2)f(z) for i<=h and zero otherwise. The structural dependence graph is the h-unit clique plus isolated diagonal vertices, so dAvg=Dbar and dMax=h. Outcomes and forced outcomes are uniformly bounded by one. The normalized centered HT estimator is exactly f, with masses (1/4,1/2,1/4), so this instance satisfies even the requested output properties. The finite sharpLaw mean zero and variance 1/2 compile in scratch/Check.lean. This construction is an example, not a substitute for the theorem's quantification over all regular Bernoulli sequences.
